prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on what matters most to you (fast emergency response, lowest price, long warranties, brand expertise, etc.). I can’t definitively pick one single company for all situations, but I can help you find the right contractor. Two quick options:

- If you want me to find nearby, highly rated options, tell me your Houston ZIP code (or neighborhood) and whether this is an emergency.
- If you want to pick on your own, use the checklist and short vendor list below.

Quick starter list (well-known companies with Houston presence — verify for your area):
- John Moore Services (Houston-based, long-running local company)
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (national franchise with local branches)
- One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning (franchise with Houston service)
- Service Experts / Aire Serv (national chains with local operations)
- ABC Home & Commercial Services (has a Houston division)

How to choose the best one for your needs
1. Licensing & certification
   - Verify they’re licensed to work in Texas / registered with TDLR for HVAC work.
   - Make sure technicians have EPA 608 certification for refrigerants.
2. Reviews & reputation
   - Check Google, Yelp, BBB, Nextdoor, and Angi/HomeAdvisor for recent reviews.
3. Pricing & estimates
   - Get at least 2–3 written estimates. Watch for unusually low bids.
   - Ask about diagnostic fees, flat-rate pricing, and exact parts vs labor costs.
4. Warranties & parts
   - Confirm parts and labor warranty length and whether they honor manufacturer warranties.
5. Response time & availability
   - If it’s an emergency, confirm 24/7 availability and typical arrival window.
6. Experience with your system
   - Ask if they’ve serviced your system brand/model before and whether they charge extra for certain brands.
7. Insurance & guarantees
   - Confirm they carry liability insurance and offer satisfaction guarantees.
8. Payment & financing
   - Check payment options, financing plans, and service/maintenance agreements.

Immediate troubleshooting (if your AC is down right now)
- Check thermostat settings and batteries.
- Replace/inspect air filter.
- Check circuit breaker at main panel and outdoor unit disconnect.
- See if outdoor condenser is running or frozen (stop and call pro if frozen).
If those don’t help, it’s reasonable to call a reputable company for diagnosis.

If you tell me your ZIP code and whether this is an urgent repair, I’ll pull 3–5 highly rated nearby contractors and list their contact info, average review scores, and any red flags.
